extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, partner organisations, donors, practitioners and the general public interested in agrifood systems and food security
extracted.subtask_description: High-level collection of FAO's stated priorities, standards and programmatic goals for building sustainable, inclusive and resilient agrifood systems globally. Covers policy guidance, standards, data/transparency, and sectoral interventions (water, fisheries, gender, climate, rural infrastructure, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy and programme design to end hunger
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO supports governments and partners to design the right policies and programmes to end hunger, promote food security and promote sustainable agriculture for millions of people around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises policy design as central to ending hunger and achieving sustainable agriculture at scale; implies programmes should be targeted, appropriate to context, and oriented to food security outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to food (access and empowerment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to food is about giving people access to enough nutritious food and empowering them to be able to feed themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames food policy around both immediate access to nutritious food and longer-term empowerment/self-sufficiency; suggests interventions should combine direct food access and capacity-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empowerment of marginalized people to end rural poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO works with governments and partners to empower some of the world’s most marginalized people to end rural poverty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on inclusion and empowerment as methods for poverty reduction; programmes should prioritise the most marginalised rural groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future-proofing food production
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO helps ensure food security by developing ways of growing food that will work in the future so that millions of people don’t go hungry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages innovation and sustainable practices that maintain productivity under future pressures (climate, resource constraints); implies long-term resilience is a success metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food quality and safety standards across the food chain
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO sets global standards and works with governments and the private sector to ensure food quality and safety throughout the food chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for regulatory and private-sector coordination across the entire value chain to maintain quality and safety; suggests adherence to international standards and collaborative implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in rural education and school meals
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO invests in educational systems for rural communities and supports improved access to primary education and school meals in order to create equal opportunities and chances of lifelong learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions education and school feeding as tools for nutrition, equality and long-term development; programmes should link education access with nutrition interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote gender equality in agriculture
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO supports gender equality in the agricultural sector in an effort to raise levels of nutrition in local communities and improve agricultural productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender-responsive programming is required to improve nutrition and productivity; interventions should address barriers faced by women farmers and promote equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient, equitable and environmentally friendly water use in agriculture
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO works with governments to ensure water use in agriculture is made more efficient, equitable and environmentally friendly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Water policy and investments should balance efficiency, fairness of access, and environmental sustainability; implies integrated water resource management approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote renewable energy and access across the food chain
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO promotes the use of renewable energies and works to ensure access to modern energy services across the food chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages adoption of renewable energy solutions at multiple nodes of the value chain to improve sustainability and access to services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in sustainable agricultural practices to create decent jobs and reduce inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO seeks better economic opportunities for all by investing in sustainable agricultural practices and food systems that reduce inequalities and create decent jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes should target both environmental sustainability and socio-economic outcomes (employment, inequality reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural infrastructure investments for community resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO seeks to secure a future for rural communities via investments in transportation, irrigation, food storage facilities and communication technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infrastructure investments should improve market access, reduce post-harvest losses, and strengthen resilience of rural livelihoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate rural employment, resource access and market connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO works with countries and partners to generate employment in rural areas, ensure access to natural resources for the most vulnerable and connect farmers to markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventions should promote inclusive access to resources and link producers to markets to improve incomes and livelihoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve urban health, water quality and city-region food systems
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO works to improve urban healthcare, water quality and rethink city region food systems to help deter the negative effects of sprawling urbanisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Urban-rural linkages and city-region planning are important to mitigate urbanisation challenges; programmes should address health, water and food-system planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tackle food waste and loss through coordinated initiatives and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO coordinates major global initiatives and projects to tackle food waste and loss, partnering with international organisations, the private sector and civil society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multistakeholder coordination is central; interventions span prevention, recovery and redistribution, involving public and private actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support climate change response with advice, data and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO supports countries in responding to the threats of climate change by providing advice, data and tools for better agricultural policies and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises evidence-based policy guidance and technical tools to enable climate-adaptive agricultural practices and policymaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fisheries best practices to protect oceans and livelihoods
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO, in partnership with governments and fishing communities, implements best practices in fisheries to ensure our oceans are protected as a means of livelihoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustainable fisheries management should balance conservation and livelihoods through community partnership and best-practice implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainable natural resource management balancing conservation and development
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO promotes sustainable approaches to natural resource management and supports endeavours that promote a balance between conservation and development initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should seek integrated outcomes that reconcile environmental conservation with development needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peacebuilding, livelihood restoration, resilience and participatory policymaking
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO plays a critical role in peacebuilding, restoring rural livelihoods, building resilience and participatory approaches to policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventions in fragile contexts should combine livelihood restoration, resilience-building and inclusive decision-making to support peace and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral forum and partnership development for consensus-building
rubrics_metrics.description: FAO acts as a neutral policymaking forum and develops partnerships with all concerned with food and agriculture to ensure a world free from hunger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neutrality and convening power are used to build consensus; partnership development across stakeholders is a core operational principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency through programme, budget and HR dashboards
rubrics_metrics.description: The enhanced FAO Transparency Portal provides dashboards on programme, budget and HR, alongside updated project data, for deeper insights into how FAO works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency and open data on programmes, budgets and human resources are expected to improve accountability and stakeholder trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize statistical processes with emphasis on emergency contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAO Data Lab for Statistical Innovation modernizes the statistical business process, with a specific focus on emergency contexts when having access to timely information is very important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical innovation and timely data provision are priorities, especially for emergency response and decision-making.
